sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Ewing Township different?
sections.html:
Ewing will not let a house change hands until it has passed a township housing inspection. For a fast sale, timing depends on how soon the property clears that check. After that, the process is the usual New Jersey deed, transfer fee and tax filings.

Ewing borders the Delaware and lies just north and west of Trenton, in Mercer County, across roughly 15.6 square miles. The 2020 count was 37,264 residents, the most the township has ever recorded, with an estimated 39,030 in 2025, a gain of 4.5 percent. Blocks near the Trenton line feel urban, but the bulk of the township is subdivisions built in separate phases, and styles shift noticeably between them.

Neighborhood names show up in listings and appraisals, so use the local one: Ewingville, West Trenton, Prospect Heights, Fernwood, Hillwood Lakes, Parkway Village, Scudders Falls or Wilburtha.

Ewing prices sit below the national median value, and renters make up about a third of households (2020 to 2024 estimates).

sections.h2: Roads and rail near Ewing homes
sections.html:
Four main roads run through Ewing, with the West Trenton rail terminal handling commuters. Interstate 295 clips the northwest corner, Route 29 follows the Delaware River as the Delaware River Scenic Byway, U.S. Route 206 skirts the southeast, and Route 31 (Pennington Road) heads north to Pennington and Flemington.

West Trenton station is the end of SEPTA's West Trenton Line, which mainly carries riders to Philadelphia. NJ Transit buses 601, 607, 608, 609 and 624 connect the township with Trenton, and Trenton-Mercer Airport sits inside the borders.

A strip of land beside the Delaware and Raritan Canal belongs to the state park of that name. Houses on River Road and Route 29 are near the water. If a buyer asks about flooding, confirm the flood-zone status with the township first.

Rain is frequent in Ewing, so inspectors look hard at grading, drainage, roofs, gutters and foundation walls. Pointing a downspout away from the foundation costs little and takes an easy objection off the table.

sections.h2: What does Ewing's resale inspection check?
sections.html:
Every dwelling or commercial building offered for resale must be inspected and approved by the Ewing Division of Housing. The residential fee on the township's 2025 form is $125. Inspectors apply the International Property Maintenance Code plus township ordinances. To book one, use the township's SDL portal (an account is required) or visit the Construction Office at 1666 Pennington Road, phone 609-883-2900, extension 7676.

The township's checklist covers more than this, but these items come up often:

  • Smoke alarms on each floor, using ten-year sealed lithium battery single-station units, and carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas.
  • A portable fire extinguisher rated at least 2A-10B:C within 10 feet of the kitchen, mounted no higher than 5 feet, and tagged or receipted within the last 12 months.
  • Ground-fault outlets in the kitchen, baths and outdoors, and no fewer than two receptacles in each bedroom.
  • Sound handrails, stairs, roofs, windows with screens, and working heating equipment.
  • No double-keyed deadbolts, which the form calls illegal.
  • Every open permit closed out, plus a well water certificate if the house has a well.

Some repairs need Uniform Construction Code permits, so phone the office before hiring a contractor.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house in Ewing
sections.html:
A rental brings more paperwork, so sort out its registration before you sell. Under township ordinance 10-07, residential rentals must be registered every year regardless of tenant changes. The registration and rental fire prevention forms are due January 31. Landlords also need a property maintenance inspection whenever a tenant changes.

Give the buyer the registration record, the newest fire prevention form and any open violation notices. Someone buying to move in will need the tenants out on a date set in the contract.

sections.h2: Closing costs and recording in Ewing
sections.html:
The Realty Transfer Fee is the seller's cost. The deed goes to the Mercer County Clerk in Trenton, where land records date back to 1838. When the total price is $350,000 or less, the state schedule is $2.00 per $500 up to $150,000, $3.35 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000 and $3.90 per $500 from $200,000 to $350,000. Ask the closing attorney for the final figure.

Recording a regular deed costs $43 for page one and $10 for every extra page. Payment of the transfer fee is accepted in cash, by cashier's check or money order, or from an attorney trust or business escrow account. Anything over $10,000 needs a certified or bank check. For sales of $1 million and up, the fee known as the mansion tax shifted to the seller on July 10, 2025.

State residents sign the GIT/REP-3 at the closing table. An owner living out of state prepays at least 2 percent of the price unless an exemption applies.

sections.h2: Steps for a quick sale in Ewing
sections.html:
The inspection sets your timeline, so book it first, through the portal or the Construction Office. Ask what the inspector will check at your address. Handle the cheap fixes yourself: alarms, extinguisher, outlets and handrails. Close open permits, and get the well water certificate if you have a well.

After the Division of Housing signs off, your closing attorney drafts the deed and the transfer fee and GIT/REP paperwork. Take the deed, your newest tax bill and a mortgage payoff figure to the first meeting. A cash buyer may accept the house as is, yet the township approval and state filings remain part of the sale.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required to sell a house in Ewing?
faqs.a: Yes. The Division of Housing inspects and approves every dwelling offered for resale. The 2025 form lists a $125 residential fee. Book through the SDL portal, or call the Construction Office at 609-883-2900, extension 7676.

faqs.q: What alarms does a Ewing resale inspection require?
faqs.a: Expect to need ten-year sealed lithium battery smoke alarms on each floor, along with carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of bedrooms. You also need a labeled fire extinguisher near the kitchen that is tagged or receipted within 12 months.

faqs.q: How much does the Mercer County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Recording costs $43 for the first page of a regular deed and $10 per added page. The transfer fee is a separate payment tied to the sale price, due when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental before selling it in Ewing?
faqs.a: Registration is yearly under ordinance 10-07, with forms due January 31, so it should already be on file. Landlords also need a property maintenance inspection on each tenant change. Have the paperwork ready so the buyer sees a clean record.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ewing house with open permits?
faqs.a: Not for long. The house cannot pass the resale inspection until open permits are closed. The Construction Office can tell you which final inspections are still outstanding, and new repairs may need their own permits first.
